name: Qwen Code

surfaces.label: Qwen Code Desktop (Tauri shell; runs a bundled `qwen serve` daemon as its child). Matched on the space-split ps argv[0] '/Applications/Qwen' plus the argument 'Desktop.app/Contents/...', because the app folder name contains spaces
qwen from npm or Homebrew: node running the bin symlink (.../bin/qwen -> cli-entry.js)
qwen from the standalone archive: bundled node running lib/cli-entry.js (bun flavour: bun)

node run directly on the bundled cli.js: the relaunch child of a TUI session (its argv[1] is cli.js, not the bin symlink) or a one-shot -p run that execve replaced the launcher. npm, Homebrew and managed-update installs only; the standalone archive's lib/cli.js is not matched
qwen serve: local HTTP daemon (Web Shell, SDKs), npm or Homebrew launch
qwen serve from the standalone archive (node or bun running <root>/lib/cli-entry.js serve). The Desktop app's own daemon is reached through the GUI surface, not this one

qwen --acp: Agent Client Protocol child, spawned by qwen serve as `node <cli.js> --acp` (argv[1] is the bundled cli.js path) or by an editor that runs the qwen binary directly. Needs 'qwen' in some argument
Qwen Code Companion in VS Code (publisher qwenlm): the editor's own Electron binary running the bundled cli.js --acp --channel=VSCode with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1

pid_index.note: Not in the schema. Two JSON files map a live PID to its session without argv, which a plain `qwen` launch never carries.
pid_index.runtime_sidecar: ~/.qwen/projects/*/chats/{session_id}.runtime.json  keys: schema_version, pid, session_id, work_dir, hostname, started_at, qwen_version. Interactive TUI only. Never deleted, so check the pid is alive.
pid_index.session_registry: ~/.qwen/sessions/<pid>.json (ACP children: <pid>-<8hex>.json)  keys: schemaVersion, pid, procStart, pidNs, sessionId, cwd, name, startedAt, qwenVersion, kind (tui|headless|serve|external), ipcPath. Unlinked on exit.
pid_index.home_override: QWEN_HOME moves ~/.qwen, including ~/.qwen/sessions. QWEN_RUNTIME_DIR moves the runtime base (projects/<slug>/chats, tmp, debug logs and other runtime output) but not ~/.qwen/sessions or settings
pid_index.project_dir: <cwd with every non-alphanumeric character replaced by '-'>, e.g. /Users/me/x -> -Users-me-x

session_store.glob_note: glob also matches sidecars <session_id>.ledger.jsonl in the same chats folder; only per_session is exact. Archived sessions live in chats/archive/.

working_signals.name: caffeinate
working_signals.meaning: Qwen Code runs `caffeinate -is` while it streams a model response or executes a tool (general.preventSystemSleep, default true, read at startup; off in --safe-mode). Not held at the idle prompt or during a permission prompt. It can drop for an instant between the end of a stream and the start of a tool, so debounce. If the user sets preventSystemSleep=false this signal is absent and only the two below remain.

Bursty. Records are queued when the prompt is accepted and when an assistant turn or tool result completes; the assistant turn is recorded after the stream ends, not while it streams. A stale file does not prove idle.
Inferred, not measured. The Ink UI redraws its spinner during a turn.

waiting_signals.meaning: A tool call needs approval. Hook input also carries session_id and transcript_path.
Fires when the permission dialog is shown; matcher is the tool id.
The turn ended and the agent is waiting for the next prompt.

OSC title is prefixed with a half-filled circle while responding, a sparkle asterisk while WaitingForConfirmation, and no prefix when idle. OSC 0 and OSC 2 outside tmux/screen, OSC 2 only inside a multiplexer. Read from the terminal emulator, not ps. Not written when ui.hideWindowTitle is true; the prefix is dropped when ui.showStatusInTitle is false.

During a permission prompt the caffeinate child is not held, per the setting description. Inferred use: a turn that started but has no caffeinate child, no CPU and a stale transcript is probably blocked on the human.

Terminal bell when an approval is needed while the terminal is unfocused (skipped when general.notificationMode is task-complete), and when a turn that ran 20 seconds or more ends while unfocused. Gated by general.terminalBell, default true. No file or process trace.

hooks.config: hooks object in ~/.qwen/settings.json, <project>/.qwen/settings.json (trusted folders only) or system /Library/Application Support/QwenCode/settings.json (override QWEN_CODE_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH); system-defaults.json in the same folder. Types: command, http, prompt, function. disableAllHooks turns them off. Commands get QWEN_PROJECT_DIR (and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR).

telemetry.how: Off by default. QWEN_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true (or --telemetry, telemetry.enabled). OTLP grpc (default) or http, default endpoint http://localhost:4317 via QWEN_TELEMETRY_OTLP_ENDPOINT / QWEN_TELEMETRY_OTLP_PROTOCOL; QWEN_TELEMETRY_OUTFILE writes a file instead. Logs, metrics and traces. Events include qwen-code.user_prompt, qwen-code.tool_call, qwen-code.api_request, qwen-code.conversation_finished. logPrompts defaults to true.

notes: Never run against a live instance. (1) Best working signal: a `caffeinate -is` child under the session, which Qwen Code holds while streaming or running a tool. It is on by default but the user can turn it off, and it flaps briefly between stream end and tool start. (2) Best pid-to-session map: read ~/.qwen/sessions/<pid>.json (sessionId, cwd, kind); it is unlinked on exit. runtime.json in the chats folder does the same for interactive sessions but is never deleted. Plain `qwen` has no session id in argv. (3) A session is one or two node processes. The launcher shows `node .../bin/qwen` (confirmed to survive a symlinked shebang launch); the relaunch child shows `node [--max-old-space-size=..] .../@qwen-code/qwen-code/cli.js` because cli-entry.js rewrites argv[1]. Keep the outermost, as the probe does. On the standalone archive the relaunch child (lib/cli.js) and a -p run that execve replaced the launcher are not matched. tool_children is left out of working_signals because MCP servers and the relaunch child are always children. (4) Desktop: shell -> `qwen serve` daemon -> `qwen --acp` children, all in one tree; the GUI shell is the outermost match. Daemon sessions register with kind serve and slot ids <pid>-<8hex>.json. (5) The probe's args_contain is substring per argument, so 'bin/qwen' and 'serve' can false-match other node tools; and path_contains looks at argv[0] only after splitting ps args on spaces, which is why the VS Code surface uses '/Applications/Visual' (this also covers Visual Studio Code - Insiders, but not Cursor or Windsurf) and the Desktop surface uses '/Applications/Qwen' plus 'Desktop.app/Contents/'. Another app under /Applications/Qwen* is excluded because it lacks the 'Desktop.app/Contents/' argument. `bin/qwen` also matches names like bin/qwen-proxy, and qwen subcommands run as helpers (mcp, review) look like sessions; the probe cannot anchor a needle. --resume=<id> and --session-id=<id> written with = are not read by session_id_args, and `-r` with no id makes the probe take the next argument as the id. (6) Headless -p runs match the tui surfaces and simply count as working for their lifetime.
